question: Which two languages got the Classical language status in 2008?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannada and Telugu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kannada** is a Dravidian language spoken predominantly by people of Karnataka in the southwestern region of India.
 
• **Telugu** is another Dravidian language spoken in the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
 
• Both Kannada and Telugu were given the status of **Classical languages in 2008** by the Government of India.
 
• Classical language status is granted to languages which have a rich heritage and independent nature, and meet certain criteria set by the Ministry of Culture in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Language Status**

 
 
• The Government of India awards the Classical Language status to languages that have a rich historical and cultural heritage.
 
• To be considered for Classical Language status, a language must have a recorded history of over 1500-2000 years, have a body of ancient literature/texts, and possess an original literary tradition that is not borrowed from another speech community.
 
• Languages that have been conferred this status receive financial assistance for setting up study centers dedicated to the language and for the development of its literature.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Languages**
 
 
• Dravidian languages form a family of languages spoken mainly in southern India and parts of eastern and central India.
 
• There are around 80 languages in this family, with the major ones being Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam.
 
• These languages have a distinct script and rich literary traditions dating back several centuries.
 
 
 
• **Kannada**
 
 
• Kannada is spoken by approximately 44 million people.
 
• The earliest examples of Kannada literature date back to the 9th century.
 
• The language has a rich literary tradition with significant contributions in poetry, drama, and prose.
 
 
 
• **Telugu**
 
 
• Telugu is spoken by over 75 million people.
 
• It is one of the classical languages of India, with a rich literary history that dates back to the 2nd century BCE.
 
• Telugu literature has a vast array of works ranging from classical poetry to modern novels and plays.
